headline: The RBI announces its rate decision at 10:00 am, and most economists expect its first rate hike since 2023. The market is likely to open lower: GIFT Nifty points to about 100 points down, close to the 22,700 floor.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: The dashboard's bias score is +6 out of 100, which counts as Neutral, because a weak price trend is cancelled out by bullish option and sentiment readings.

key_points.text: The RBI decides on rates at 10:00 am. In a Business Standard poll, 8 of 10 economists expect a rise from 5.25% to **5.50%**, so a hike is mostly expected. The bigger risk is a tougher message about more hikes to come.
GIFT Nifty, which trades overnight and hints at the opening price, was at **22,674** at 8 am, about 0.4% below Tuesday's close. That would undo about half of Tuesday's 1% rise.

Nifty is still below all three of its average prices (20, 50 and 200 days), so the bigger trend is down. But option sellers moved their floor up to **22,700**, which suggests they see support close below the price.
Foreign investors (FIIs) sold ₹2,961 crore of shares on Tuesday, but Indian funds (DIIs) bought **₹5,089 crore**. Local buying is currently soaking up all of the foreign selling.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is down, but the last two days and the options market show buyers fighting back.

points.text: The data shows Nifty closed at 22,776 on Tuesday, up **0.98%**, its second day of gains, after a low of 22,422 on 1 October.
Nifty is below its 20-day (23,147), 50-day (23,824) and 200-day (24,318) averages, and recent peaks and dips are both getting lower. The trend step scores **−2**, its weakest possible reading.
Option sellers added large new bets that Nifty stays above 22,500 and 22,600, and the floor moved up from 22,500 to **22,700**. The option chain step scores +1.5.

The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) climbed from 0.71 to **1.06** in five days. The dashboard reads this as people becoming more willing to bet that the market won't fall further, and scores it +1.
India VIX, the market's fear gauge, is 13.6, higher than on **64%** of days in the past year. Options are fairly priced, neither cheap nor expensive.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign investors are still selling and still betting on a fall, while Indian funds keep buying.

points.text: News reports say FIIs have sold about **₹17,145 crore** in the first three trading days of October. Our own dashboard history covers only Tuesday so far.
Indian funds bought more than ₹20,312 crore over the same three days, per the same reports. That is the main reason falls have been limited.
In index futures, only **8.5%** of FII positions are bets on a rise. That is very low, which means they are still heavily betting on a fall.
That share rose slightly from 8.0% to 8.5%. Readings under 10% have often come before FIIs buy back their bets on a fall, which pushes prices up. The rise is still too small to count as that turn.
In the second half of September, FIIs sold the most in financial companies (**₹6,943 crore**), then oil and gas, and then autos (NSDL data).

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: US stocks are at record highs, but high oil, high US interest rates and a weak rupee still weigh on India.

points.text: The S&P 500 rose **0.6%** to a record high on Tuesday, led by tech stocks as oil prices eased (TheStreet). However, Asian markets were lower this morning.
Brent crude is about **$101** a barrel, 29% higher than three months ago, because of attacks on Middle East oil routes. India buys most of its oil from abroad, so expensive oil hurts India.
Oil is down about 4% this week. Saudi Aramco cut its price for Asian buyers, and Gulf shipping is recovering. If that continues, it would help India.
The US 10-year bond pays **5.28%**, near its highest level in a year, and the rupee is close to a record low at about 96.3 per dollar. Both make India less attractive to foreign investors.

US short-term bond rates suggest traders still expect the US central bank (the Fed) to raise rates, but that expectation eased this week. Notes from the Fed's last meeting come out tonight at 11:30 pm IST.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No Nifty 50 company reported this week, and the real results season starts with TCS on Thursday.

points.text: The 20 filings from the last 7 days are all small companies. Most don't include last year's figures, so they tell us little about the market.
TCS reports on **8 October**. Its share price fell 14.5% in September, and Kotak expects only about 0.5% revenue growth over the previous quarter.
HCL Tech reports on 12 October, and HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank on 17 October. Bank results matter most, because FIIs have been selling financial stocks.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: Today's RBI decision and the next few days of data and results will decide which way the market breaks.

points.text: If the RBI raises rates and hints at more, banks and rate-sensitive stocks could fall. A hike with a calm message could bring relief, since it is mostly expected.
India's inflation figure comes out on **12 October**. Inflation was 4.82% in August, and a higher number would add to fears of more rate hikes.
My read would turn more positive if FIIs' share of bets on a rise climbs clearly above 10% and Nifty closes above **23,000**.
My read would turn more negative if Nifty closes below 22,700, because that would mean the new floor failed on its first test.

levels.note: A close above 23,000 would push past the biggest wall of bets against a rise. A close below 22,700 would break the floor that option sellers just built, and the next support would be near 22,500.

watch.text: Opening price: does Nifty open near 22,670, as GIFT Nifty suggests, and does it hold above 22,700?
RBI rate decision and statement. A hike to 5.50% is expected, so the tone of the statement matters more than the hike itself.
RBI governor's press conference, for any comments on the rupee, inflation or further hikes (usual timing, not confirmed for today).
Evening FII and DII flow figures: does local buying keep outweighing foreign selling?
Notes from the US Fed's last meeting. Talk of higher rates would push US bond rates and the dollar up.

bottom_line: The dashboard reads the market as Neutral with low confidence: the price trend is clearly down, but option sellers and the put-call ratio point to support around 22,700. Indian funds are buying more than foreign investors are selling, which has stopped the fall for now, but foreign investors have not yet bought back their bets on a fall. The main risk is the RBI's tone at 10:00 am. A tougher message than expected, along with a weak start from GIFT Nifty, could push Nifty below 22,700 and the trend step would be proved right again.
